title: Precision metering probe: directional per-token fairness
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers report unpredictable bill moves when chat apps switch between high-ingress short prompts and high-egress long responses (e.g., retrieval-heavy assistants). Current symmetric per-token pricing biases certain workloads and discourages streaming adoption due to minimums and rounding.

Goal: Run a controlled probe to test directional metering (separate ingress vs egress rates with fairness adjustments) and a short streaming grace window to reduce bill spikes while preserving revenue neutrality. Evaluate impact on usage behavior, unit economics, and churn.

Hypotheses:
1) Separating ingress/output rates (e.g., cheaper input tokens) will encourage customers to offload more compute to prompts and reduce served output length, shifting model selection patterns.
2) A 3-second streaming grace window that temporarily suspends minimum-quantization rounding will reduce surprise bills for chaty workloads without materially decreasing revenue (target ±5%).
3) Combined directional metering + grace window will increase streaming adoption by ~8% among active customers in the test cohort.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment runs 4 weeks with 10k eligible customers traffic split into control and two treatment arms
Billing infra reports ingress and egress tokens separately in daily aggregates and per-route breakdowns
Revenue delta across treatment arms within ±5% vs control or documented compensating pricing adjustments approved
At least one actionable change recommended (pricing tweak, docs update, or rollout plan) based on results
No customer support escalations > P2 attributable to billing changes during the probe
metrics: Primary: net revenue per active user (NRPU) — daily and weekly windows
Secondary: streaming sessions started per week, avg output length (tokens), avg input length (tokens)
Tertiary: churn propensity signals (downgrades/cancellation), support ticket volume referencing billing surprises
experiment_design: Cohort selection: active hosted API customers with >=5000 tokens/month and at least 30 streaming sessions in last 30 days

Arms: Control (current pricing); T1 directional: input tokens billed at 0.6x output rate; T2 directional+grace: same rates + 3s streaming grace window that defers rounding minimums for the first 3s of a stream
Randomization: user-level randomization with stratification on monthly spend bucket and vertical tag
Duration: 4 weeks data collection, 2 weeks analysis
Instrumentation: add per-request ingress/egress token counters, experiment flag in logs, and per-user cohort labels in billing export
implementation_notes: Requires billing pipeline change: split token counters early in request path and persist per-direction counters to event log
Backend: small hook in proxy to mark stream start times for grace-window evaluation (ENG-22145 ownership)
Data: export to analytics bigquery table with schema (date, customer_id, cohort, ingress_tokens, egress_tokens, cost_calc) for daily rollups
Promo: allocate a temporary credit budget for sample customers to avoid negative surprises during early bug fixes
Engineering PR: redwood/billing#987 (draft) implements split-counting and per-direction ledger entries
risks_mitigations: Risk: Customers see unexpected lower/higher bills leading to support spikes. Mitigation: pre-notify test cohort by email and in-console banner; enable quick rollback flag
Risk: Revenue erosion if customers game ingress/egress split. Mitigation: cap per-minute ingress discounts and monitor outliers, add rate limits in detection window
Risk: Misattribution due to seasonality. Mitigation: run stratified cohorts and compare multiple weeks of lookback
Risk: Implementation bugs in meter counting. Mitigation: shadow deploy with mirrored counting for 48 hours and reconcile totals before enabling billing
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (shadow): 2026-03-01 — split counting in shadow for 48hrs and reconcile totals
Phase 1 (pilot): 2026-03-08 — enable T1 for 1k customers, monitor 72hrs
Phase 2 (pilot+grace): 2026-03-15 — enable T2 for 1k different customers, monitor 7 days
Phase 3 (full probe): 2026-03-22 — expand to full 10k cohort; collect 4 weeks of signals
Rollback: global feature flag to revert cohort billing to control immediately; legal notified on rollback
